## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sukkadhamma Sutta* ("Bright Things", Iti 42, PTS It 36) is the fifteenth discourse in the second chapter (*Dukanipāta*) of the *Itivuttaka*. The discourse teaches that two bright qualities (*sukkā dhammā*)—namely conscience (*hiri*) and prudence or moral shame (*ottappa*)—serve as guardians that safeguard the world (*dve'me bhikkhave sukkā dhammā lokaṃ pālenti*) [de La Vallée Poussin 1903]. Without these two protective principles, moral order would disintegrate and human beings would fail to respect familial and social boundaries.

  DharmaNexus also detects shared segments with the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā*, *Majjhimanikāya-aṭṭhakathā*, *Abhidhammāvatāra-purāṇaṭīkā*, and another *Itivuttaka* text (Iti 31, *Ātapanīya Sutta*), alongside cross-language alignments with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) and *Ekottarikāgama* (T 125) [DharmaNexus].
